deep.reconstruction:
The page is not in Riemann's hand. It is a draft by Richard Dedekind of the end of his 'Erläuterungen zu den vorstehenden Fragmenten' (Riemann, Werke, 1876, commentary to Fragment XXVIII on the limiting cases of the elliptic modular functions). It is filed in Riemann's Nachlass. The wording shows this: 'die Riemann'schen Formeln', and on the previous page 'der von Riemann angewendeten ... Methode'.

Context from the previous page. (m,n) is Dedekind's integer symbol that appears in the transformation law of log η(ω) under (aω+b)/(cω+d); here n plays the role of c. The previous page derives
  (m,n)πi/6 = Σ_ν a⁰_ν/ν,
where a⁰_ν is periodic mod n with Σ_{ν=1}^n a⁰_ν = 0. Dirichlet's method (1/ν = ∫_0^1 x^{ν-1}dx, then partial fractions) turns this into
  (m,n)πi/6 = -Σ_{t≢0 mod n} f(α^{-mt}) log(1-α^{mt}),
with α = e^{2πi/n} (implicit) and f(x) = Σ_{ν=1}^n a⁰_ν x^ν. Writing a⁰_ν as a finite Fourier sum gives f(α^{-mt}) = |-t| - |t|, where |t| is the least nonnegative residue of t mod n. The branch of the logarithm is fixed by Im log(1-α^{mt}) = π((mt/n - 1/2)). Here ((x)) denotes the representative of x mod 1 lying between ±1/2.

This page (my filling of steps).
(1) Write log(1-α^{mt}) = log|1-α^{mt}| + πi((mt/n-1/2)). This follows from 1-e^{iθ} = -2i sin(θ/2) e^{iθ/2}.
(2) The coefficient |-t|-|t| is odd under t → -t, while log|1-α^{mt}| is even. So the real parts cancel in the sum.
(3) Dividing the remaining imaginary part by πi gives Dedekind's first finite formula:
  (m,n)/6 = Σ_{t mod n} (|t| - |-t|) ((mt/n - 1/2)).
  The t ≡ 0 term vanishes because its coefficient is 0.
(4) For 1 ≤ t ≤ n-1, |t| - |-t| = t - (n-t) = 2t - n = 2n(t/n - 1/2) = 2n((t/n - 1/2)). This gives
  (m,n)/6 = 2n Σ_t ((t/n - 1/2))((mt/n - 1/2)).
(5) For non-integer x, ((x - 1/2)) = {x} - 1/2. This is the modern sawtooth ((x)). So the formula reads (m,n) = 12n·s(m,n), where s(m,n) = Σ_{t=1}^{n-1} ((t/n))((mt/n)) is the Dedekind sum.

The text then remarks that this finite expression can be transformed and much simplified (in the published version this leads to reciprocity), 'was aber hier unterbleiben soll'. It also says that deriving Riemann's formulas for log k, log k', log(2K/π) would 'go too far'. These follow easily, since k, k', K are reduced to η, and log η(2ω), log η(ω/2), log η((1+ω)/2) follow from the η-transformation once the three parity cases of (m,n) mod 2 are separated.

Purpose: an explicit finite (Dedekind-sum) expression for the constant in the η-multiplier. This is the birth of Dedekind sums.
errors: Second expression 2n Σ((t/n-1/2))((mt/n-1/2)): if t ≡ 0 is included, the term ((-1/2))^2 = 1/4 adds n/2 (and ((-1/2)) is ambiguous under the convention 'between ±1/2'). The t ≡ 0 term must be excluded or the convention ((integer)) = 0 adopted. The first expression is unaffected because its coefficient is 0 there. This is a minor notational slip.
The cancellation of the real parts log|1-α^{mt}| (odd coefficient times even function) is used tacitly and not stated.
α = e^{2πi/n} is implicit; in the draft the sign/orientation conventions are carried from the previous page and not restated.

results.what: Finite-sum formula for the η-multiplier constant: (m,n)/6 = Σ(|t|-|-t|)((mt/n-1/2)) = 2n Σ((t/n))((mt/n)), i.e. (m,n) = 12 n s(m,n)
results.modern_name: Dedekind sum s(m,n) in the transformation formula of the Dedekind eta function
results.usually_credited_to: R. Dedekind, Erläuterungen to Riemann's fragment XXVIII (Riemann Werke 1876; 2nd ed. 1892)

results.what: Evaluation of the periodic series Σ a_ν/ν by Dirichlet's method (integral representation, partial fractions, logarithms at roots of unity) with branch Im log(1-e^{2πix}) = π({x}-1/2)
results.modern_name: Evaluation of L-type series with periodic coefficients via finite Fourier analysis

results.what: Remark that Riemann's formulas for log k, log k', log(2K/π) follow from the η-transformation by splitting cases of m,n mod 2
results.modern_name: Expressions of elliptic modulus and complete integral via eta quotients (Weber functions)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of Dedekind's well-known published commentary in Riemann's Werke, where Dedekind sums first appear. It is not Riemann's own mathematics, and its content matches the published text, which is already credited to Dedekind.

transcription_corrections: The hand is Dedekind's (draft of his Erläuterungen), not Riemann's.

'was aber hier unterbleiben soll. Ebenso würde es zu weit führen,' is a right-margin insertion replacing the struck 'doch würde dies uns hier zu weit führen. Ebenso ist es nicht mehr möglich'; the transcription renders this correctly.
In 'Schwierigkeit [-darbieten-] {+bieten+} kann' the superscript replacement appears to read 'bieten'; plausible but uncertain.
The second expression on the first formula line is written as '= 2n Σ((t/n - 1/2))((mt/n - 1/2))'; the transcription is correct.
